terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, transitive; with ab and the ablative
evidence: Mor. 14: oppositāque manū lūmen dēfendit ab aurā
terms.comment: To protect someone from something is aliquem ab aliquā rē dēfendere; the harm kept off can also be the object, as in frīgus et sōlem dēfendere (Cato Agr. 48.2, Lewis & Short).

evidence: Phaedr. 3.7.9–10: custōs ut sīs līminis, ā fūribus tueāris et noctū domum
terms.comment: See also maintain and provide for.

evidence: Vulg. Ps. 16 (17), 8: Sub umbrā ālārum tuārum prōtege mē
Verg. G. 2.489: ingentī rāmōrum prōtegat umbrā
Vulg. Num. 6.24: Benedīcat tibi Dominus, et custōdiat tē.

terms.comment: To protect someone is also alicuī praesidiō esse (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: tandem conceptō, sed vix, fulgōre recēdit, oppositāque manū lūmen dēfendit ab aurā
phrases.english: At last, when the flame has caught (only just), he steps back and shields the light from the draught with his hand.

phrases.latin: custōdī mē ut pūpillam oculī. Sub umbrā ālārum tuārum prōtege mē
phrases.english: Keep me as the apple of your eye; protect me under the shadow of your wings.

phrases.latin: custōs ut sīs līminis, ā fūribus tueāris et noctū domum
phrases.english: Just guard the door, and keep the house safe from thieves at night.

sources: Lewis & Short: defendo · Lewis & Short: tueor · Lewis & Short: protego · Lewis & Short: custodio · Lewis & Short: praesidium
